merger_description:
Bankstown Central Property Pty Ltd as trustee for the Bankstown Central Property Unit Trust and Oscars NSW Ops Pty Ltd (the **Acquirers**) propose to acquire 100% of the freehold land interest, buildings, licenses and business assets (both tangible and intangible) of the South Terrace Hotel in Bankstown, New South Wales from MAHF Custodian Pty Ltd as custodian for RGM TT Pty Ltd as trustee for the Red Lantern Hotel Trust and Redcape Hotel Group Pty Ltd, as described in the transaction documents provided as part of the application (the **Acquisition**).

The South Terrace Hotel is a community, food, beverage and entertainment venue located at 280 South Terrace, Bankstown NSW 2200.

The Acquirers are part of the Oscars Group, which owns and operates community, food & beverage, entertainment and accommodation venues. The Oscars Group own and operate hospitality venues across New South Wales, South Australia, Queensland and Victoria.

determination_table_content.details:
Bankstown Central Property Pty Ltd as trustee for the Bankstown
Central Property Unit Trust and Oscars NSW Ops Pty Ltd (the
Acquirers) applied for a notification waiver in respect of their
proposed acquisition of the freehold land interest, buildings, licenses
and business assets (both tangible and intangible) of the South
Terrace Hotel in Bankstown, New South Wales (the South Terrace
Hotel), as described in the transaction documents provided as part
of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The Acquirers are part of the Oscars Group, which owns and
operates community, food & beverage, entertainment and
accommodation venues across New South Wales, South Australia,
Queensland and Victoria.
The target, the South Terrace Hotel, is a community, food, beverage
and entertainment venue located at 280 South Terrace, Bankstown
NSW 2200.
The parties both supply retail hospitality services including dining,
entertainment, gaming and on-premises liquor services in the City of
Canterbury Bankstown local council area.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of dining,
entertainment, gaming and on-premises liquor services at
pub-style venues in the local area surrounding the South
Terrace Hotel is low to moderate
b. there are alternative pub-style venues that supply dining,
entertainment, gaming, and liquor for on-site consumption in
the local area surrounding the South Terrace Hotel and in the
broader City of Canterbury Bankstown area.
• The ACCC has also had regard to the likelihood that, if the
Acquisition were put into effect, the notification thresholds
determined under section 51ABP(1) of the Act would apply.
While the ACCC considers that the notification thresholds are likely
to be met, given that material competition concerns are unlikely to
arise, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required
to be notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
